items.problem: On the SEQUENTIAL code-behind Scenario1.xaml.cs, the dev-agent overwrote the entire file with a here-string piped to Set-Content instead of editing the bootstrap copy in place. It was faithful only by luck (visible text lived in the .xaml, not the .cs).
items.evidence: build-events.jsonl exec #42 (backup Scenario1.xaml.cs.bak) + exec #43 (@'...full file...'@ | Set-Content Scenario1.xaml.cs -Encoding UTF8); reasoning turns 22-26. Classified in skill-coverage-gaps.json.
items.root_cause: SKILL.md's 'never wholesale-overwrite the bootstrap copy' fidelity rule is scoped only to '*.xaml'; code-behind/helper .cs files have no equivalent prohibition, and SEQUENTIAL (filtered-API) files make Set-Content the path of least resistance. The validator's verbatim-text check covers XAML only, so a .cs rewrite is unguarded.
items.change: Two surgical prose edits: (1) widen the Fidelity anti-overwrite rule from '*.xaml' to all bootstrap-copied source files (incl. *.xaml.cs and helper *.cs), noting the validator text-check is XAML-only so .cs rewrites are unguarded; (2) add a clause to the Step 1 SEQUENTIAL bullet: a filtered-API file is not a licence to wholesale-rewrite — keep editing in place, cross-linking the Fidelity rule.
items.expected_effect: On re-run, the dev-agent edits code-behind and helper .cs in place rather than overwriting them, preserving user-visible strings verbatim even on SEQUENTIAL files.
items.falsifiable_check: No `Set-Content` / here-string wholesale overwrite of a `*.cs` (or `*.xaml`) bootstrap-copied file appears in build-events.jsonl on a re-run, and Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 visible-text check stays clean; a Tier-3 (prose) change is used because a Tier-1 validator diff of arbitrary .cs verbatim text is infeasible (legitimate .cs edits are the norm).
